name: structured-data
description:
A second expression of a structure the component already draws, serialised for a reader that is not a person. APG has no pattern for one and neither does WCAG, so this is Arena's own, and it is the first pattern here that is NOT an accessibility requirement: it carries no role, answers no key, takes no focus and dismisses nothing. That is why it is additive rather than a pattern a component binds instead of its own. A component keeps the pattern that says what it does, and adds this one to say that it also writes down what it IS.

The precedent inside Arena is figure-with-data-table, and the argument transfers with one correction worth stating rather than glossing. That pattern requires a real table of the plotted numbers because a picture nobody can read is not an alternative, and its reader is a screen reader. This one's reader is a machine that never renders the page at all, so the two are not the same requirement wearing different clothes, and the honest reason they belong in the same directory is narrower: both say that a component owes a second, invisible rendering of a fact its visible one already carries.

The objection has to be answered here, because the pattern it comes from raised it first and a reviewer meeting this file will raise it again. figure-with-data-table weighed a hidden listbox mirroring the marks and refused it: it is a second copy of the same numbers in the same DOM, and one source per fact is the rule that copy would break. A JSON-LD block IS a second copy. What saves it is that the refused listbox was DOM for a screen reader competing with DOM that already served screen readers, so one of the two was redundant by construction. Nothing expresses this structure to a machine today, so this copy competes with nothing, and the rule it would break is not engaged. The test of that claim is the one to apply to any future addition here: if a reader can already get the fact, do not write it twice.

The serialisation is a surface a consumer's own strings reach, so it is a surface an attacker reaches. A label carrying the closing script tag would end the block and begin whatever follows it, which is why the requirement names the escape rather than leaving it to whoever implements the pattern next.

requires.alternative.jsonLd: a <script type="application/ld+json"> beside the component's own markup, holding a schema.org description of the same structure, with < escaped as \u003c in the serialisation so no value a consumer supplies can close the tag
